rationale: The Toronto Star's 17 May 1999 story on the Trinity—Spadina race, which Rosario Marchese won, describes the Liberal candidate Albert Koehl as a former environmental prosecutor and human rights worker. That matches the 1999 Liberal run, second of eight with 9,817 votes. The Star's 27 October 2014 story names Albert Koehl as a council candidate in Ward 20 (Trinity-Spadina) and calls him an environmental lawyer, which matches the 2014 Ward 20 run. The two stories describe the same occupation in closely related terms, and no one else in the release has the name. The 1999 Ontario legislature run and the 2014 Ward 20 council run are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada gives Ashley James Deans as the Natural Law Party of Canada candidate in Trinity—Spadina in the 1993 federal election, and Ashley Deans as the Natural Law Party candidate in Trinity—Spadina in 1997 and 2000. The 1997 riding is the successor of the 1993 riding of the same name, and no general election came between the 1993 and 1997 runs. No one else in the release has the name, and Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file lists no other Deans. Wikipedia's article on the Natural Law Party of Canada says Ashley Deans was a candidate in Trinity-Spadina in 1997 and 2000 and president of the Ontario party from 1993 to 2000, which is consistent with the 1993 run but does not name it. The link rests on same-office continuity. The 1993 Trinity—Spadina run joins the Person holding the 1997 and 2000 Trinity—Spadina runs.

Wikipedia's article on the 2020 Toronto Centre federal by-election says the Conservatives replaced their first nominee with Benjamin Sharma, who had run for the party in the 2014 Trinity—Spadina by-election, and its results give Benjamin Gauri Sharma 1,435 votes and fourth place, which matches the 2020 run. Wikipedia's page on by-elections to the 41st Parliament names Benjamin Sharma as the Conservative candidate in the June 2014 Trinity—Spadina by-election with 2,022 votes, which matches the 2014 run. The 2014 Trinity—Spadina and 2020 Toronto Centre by-election runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's biography of Chris Stockwell, the former Progressive Conservative MPP, says he was elected in his own riding in 1995 and re-elected in 1999 in the redistributed riding of Etobicoke Centre, which matches the 1995 Etobicoke West and 1999 Etobicoke Centre wins. It also says he registered in September 2014 as a candidate for Toronto City Council in Ward 4 in Etobicoke and came fourth, and its Ward 4 table gives him 2,208 votes, which matches the 2014 council run. The 2014 Ward 4 council run joins the Person holding the 1995 and 1999 Ontario legislature runs.

Wikipedia's article on Brad Duguid says Costas Manios, the Liberal candidate in the 1999 Ontario election, was expected to win the Scarborough Centre nomination again and instead ran against Duguid in 2003 as an independent, finishing fourth behind the New Democrat Michael Laxer. That matches the 2003 Scarborough Centre run, fourth of seven with no party. Wikipedia's article on Marilyn Mushinski says she was re-elected in 1999 by about 4,000 votes over the Liberal Costas Manios, with Sid Ryan third, which matches the 1999 Scarborough Centre run (18,189 votes to 14,565). The 1999 and 2003 Scarborough Centre runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's list of Marxist-Leninist candidates in the 2006 federal election has an entry for David Gershuny, the Oshawa candidate, which calls him a shipper and heavy vehicle operator and a perennial candidate for the party. Its electoral record gives his 1993 St. Paul's run with 75 votes, tenth of twelve, won by Barry Campbell, which matches the 1993 run. It also gives a 1999 provincial run as an independent Marxist-Leninist with 486 votes, fifth of eight, won by Joseph Cordiano. The table labels that riding Beaches—East York, but Cordiano won York South—Weston, where the 1999 record has David Gershuny fifth of eight with 486 votes. Elections Canada lists David Gershuny as a shipper-receiver for the 1993 St. Paul's run and again for the 2025 Toronto—St. Paul's run, both for the Marxist-Leninist Party, which matches the occupation the Wikipedia entry gives. The 1993 St. Paul's, 1999 York South—Weston and 2025 Toronto—St. Paul's runs are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada gives Elmer Gale as the Marijuana Party candidate in Davenport in the 2000 and 2004 federal elections, sixth of eight with 480 votes and fifth of eight with 251 votes. The 2004 Davenport riding is the successor of the 2000 riding of the same name, the elections are consecutive, and no one else in the release has the name. Elections Canada lists him as a school caretaker in 2000 and a door attendant in 2004, which neither confirms nor separates the runs. The link rests on same-office continuity. The 2000 and 2004 Davenport runs are joined as one Person.

Elections Ontario gives Hassan Husseini as the Communist Party of Canada (Ontario) candidate in York South—Weston in the 1999 provincial election, sixth of eight with 261 votes, and Wikipedia's page on that election lists him there. Elections Canada gives the Person holding the 1997 and 2000 federal runs as the Communist Party of Canada candidate in York South—Weston in the 2000 federal election, about eighteen months later. The runs are at both levels in a riding of the same name within two years, for the federal and Ontario parties of one name, and Hassan Husseini is an uncommon name that no other Person in the release has. The link rests on the rule for runs at both levels in one riding. The 1999 York South—Weston provincial run joins the Person holding the 1997 and 2000 federal runs.

The Canadian Jewish News, reporting Joel Etienne's 2021 Conservative candidacy against Ya'ara Saks in York Centre, describes him as a 47-year-old lawyer and says he was the Canadian Alliance candidate in Eglinton-Lawrence in the 2000 federal election. Wikipedia's list of Canadian Alliance candidates in 2000 describes the Eglinton—Lawrence candidate as a 26-year-old Toronto lawyer who received 5,497 votes and finished third against Joseph Volpe, which matches the 2000 run. Elections Canada lists the candidate as a lawyer in 2000 and in 2021. The 2000 Eglinton—Lawrence and 2021 York Centre runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's article on John C. Turmel, a perennial candidate, gives his electoral record. It lists the 25 March 1996 Etobicoke North federal by-election, where he ran for the Abolitionist Party and received 75 votes, which matches the 1996 run. It also lists the Toronto by-elections held by the other Person with totals that match the records, among them Toronto—Danforth in 2012 with 57 votes, Toronto Centre in 2013 with 56, Trinity—Spadina in 2014 with 141, Scarborough—Agincourt in 2017 with 145 and York Centre in 2020 with 104. The 1996 Etobicoke North by-election run joins the Person holding the later by-election runs.

Elections Canada gives Kingsley Kwok as the New Democratic Party candidate in Scarborough—Rouge Park in the 2019 federal election, third of six with 5,801 votes, and Kingsley Arnold Kwok as the party's candidate there in 2021, third of four with 6,068 votes, and lists the candidate as a respiratory therapist both times. The runs are for the same office and party in the same riding at consecutive general elections, under a name that no one else in the release has, which meets same-office continuity. The 2021 Scarborough—Rouge Park run joins the Person holding the 2017 Ward 42, 2019 Scarborough—Rouge Park and 2025 Scarborough—Guildwood—Rouge Park runs.

Elections Canada gives Lorne Gershuny as the Marxist-Leninist candidate in Parkdale—High Park in the 2000 federal election and in every federal election from 2004 to 2025, and lists him as a lawyer in 2000 and in each later run. The 2004 riding is the successor of the 2000 riding of the same name, the elections are consecutive, and no one else in the release has the name. The 2000 Parkdale—High Park run joins the Person holding the runs there from 2004 to 2025.

The Toronto Star's 2 June 1995 profile of the York Mills riding describes the Libertarian candidate Mark Meschino as a 37-year-old labourer with a university mathematics degree who ran and lost in the last two federal elections, which matches the 1995 York Mills run. Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file lists one Meschino in the country, Mark Meschino, the Libertarian candidate in Don Valley East, who lost, which is the 1993 run. The 1993 Don Valley East federal run and the 1995 York Mills provincial run are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's biography of Michael Laxer says he was the New Democratic Party candidate in Scarborough—Agincourt in the 2000 federal election and the Ontario NDP candidate in Scarborough Centre in the 2003 provincial election, which match the 2000 federal run and the 2003 provincial run. It also says he ran for council in Ward 6 Etobicoke—Lakeshore in 2010 and 2014 with 717 and 305 votes, which match the two council runs. The 2000 Scarborough—Agincourt run joins the Person holding the 2003 Scarborough Centre run and the 2010 and 2014 Ward 6 runs.

Wikipedia's biography of Morley Kells says he won Etobicoke—Lakeshore for the Progressive Conservatives in 1995 and was re-elected in 1999 over the Liberal Laurel Broten, which match the 1995 and 1999 wins. It says he lost to Broten by just over 5,000 votes in 2003, which matches the 2003 run (19,680 votes to 14,524), and that he ran unsuccessfully for council in Ward 5 in 2010 against Peter Milczyn, with 2,725 votes in its results table, which matches the 2010 council run. The 2003 Etobicoke—Lakeshore and 2010 Ward 5 runs join the Person holding the 1995 and 1999 Etobicoke—Lakeshore wins.

The City's results give Patrick T. McCool third of three for Metro council in Rexdale Thistletown in 1994, and Patrick McCool eleventh of twelve for the amalgamated council in Ward 5 Rexdale-Thistletown in 1997. The 1997 council was elected in the Metro wards, so both races were for the council seat of the same area in consecutive elections, and John Kiru's runs in the same two races were joined on the same basis. McCool is an uncommon name and no one else in the release has it. The link rests on same-office continuity. The 1994 Metro council run and the 1997 Ward 5 council run are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's 2 June 1995 profile of the Oriole riding describes the Progressive Conservative candidate Paul Sutherland as Deputy Mayor of North York and a fourth-term councillor, and its 5 June 1995 story lists North York councillor Paul Sutherland, the Conservative candidate in Oriole, among candidates elected to municipal councils the previous fall. That matches the 1995 Oriole run and the November 1994 North York Ward 14 win. Wikipedia's biography of Paul Sutherland gives him as the North York councillor for Ward 14 from 1985 to 1997. The 1995 Oriole run joins the Person holding the 1994 North York Ward 14, 2000 Ward 33 and 2003 Don Valley East runs.

A 2007 copy of Wikipedia's list of Family Coalition Party candidates in the 2003 Ontario election has an entry for Ray Scott, the Scarborough Southwest candidate. It says he first ran for the party in a 2001 by-election in Beaches—East York and finished fifth of eight with 206 votes in a race won by Michael Prue of the NDP, which matches the September 2001 by-election run. It gives his 2003 result as 586 votes, last of five, in a race won by Lorenzo Berardinetti, which matches the 2003 Scarborough Southwest run. The 2001 Beaches—East York by-election run and the 2003 Scarborough Southwest run are joined as one Person.

Stephen Kevins ran for the Scarborough Board of Education in Ward 7 in 1994, second of four, and Stephen M. Kevins ran for the Toronto District School Board, the Scarborough board's successor, in Ward 12 in 1997, third of four. The release has no boundaries for these wards, but its records place them in the same part of Scarborough. Candidates with the names of the 1994 Ward 7 council winner and runner-up stood in 1997 in council Ward 13 Scarborough Bluffs, and TDSB Ward 12 in 1997 was won by Elizabeth Moyer, the 1994 trustee for Scarborough Ward 2, with a namesake of the 1994 Ward 7 trustee and Kevins among the other candidates. The elections are consecutive, and no one else in the release has the name. The link rests on same-office continuity. The 1994 Scarborough Ward 7 and 1997 TDSB Ward 12 runs are joined as one Person.

A 2007 copy of Wikipedia's list of Family Coalition Party candidates in the 2003 Ontario election has an entry for Tony Ieraci, the Scarborough—Agincourt candidate, which says he ran in Broadview—Greenwood in the 1999 provincial election and received 320 votes, last of six, in a race won by Marilyn Churley of the NDP. That matches the 1999 run, which the release labels Toronto—Danforth. The entry gives his 2003 result as 550 votes, last of five, in a race won by Gerry Phillips, which matches the 2003 Scarborough—Agincourt run. The 1999 Toronto—Danforth and 2003 Scarborough—Agincourt runs are joined as one Person.

Elections Ontario gives Wayne Simmons as the Freedom Party of Ontario candidate in Don Valley East in the 1999 and 2003 provincial elections, ninth of ten with 53 votes and sixth of six with 119 votes, on the same riding boundaries with no general election between, and no one else in the release has the name. The Freedom Party's page on its 1999 campaign dinner lists Wayne Simmons as its Don Valley East candidate, and VoteMate's 2021 profile of the People's Party candidate in Toronto—Danforth, a run held by the later Person, says he joined the Freedom Party in the late 1990s and ran for it in several elections. The link rests on same-office continuity. The 1999 Don Valley East run joins the Person holding the Freedom Party runs from 2003 to 2022 and the 2021 federal run.

The Toronto Star's report on the 2000 Don Valley West result (28 November 2000) describes the NDP candidate Naqvi as 36 and an immigration and legal consultant, which is the 2000 Don Valley West run (fourth of six, 2,024 votes). The Star's story on Etobicoke North of 10 January 2006 describes the NDP candidate Ali Naqvi as 41 and an immigration consultant, which is the 2006 Etobicoke North run (third of seven, 3,820 votes), and Elections Canada gives that candidate as a legal consultant. The occupation is the same in both years and the ages agree. The 2000 Don Valley West run is joined to the Person that holds the 2003 Don Valley West provincial run and the 2006 and 2008 Etobicoke North runs.

Wikipedia's biography of Barbara Greene, the Progressive Conservative MP for Don Valley North from 1988 to 1993, says she lost to the Liberal Sarkis Assadourian in the 1993 federal election, and its results table gives her 7,238 votes, which is the 1993 Don Valley North run (second of six). It also says she ran as the provincial Progressive Conservative candidate in a 1997 by-election in the North York riding of Oriole and was defeated by the Liberal David Caplan, which is the September 1997 Oriole by-election run (second of five, behind Caplan). The 1993 Don Valley North run and the 1997 Oriole by-election run are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's biography of Bill Whatcott says he ran for the Family Coalition Party in Toronto Centre in the 1999 Ontario election and finished eighth with 232 votes, which is the 1999 Toronto Centre—Rosedale run (eighth of nine, 232 votes), and that he has repeatedly run for political office. Wikipedia's article on the April 2026 University—Rosedale federal by-election says the socially conservative perennial candidate Bill Whatcott ran as an independent, links his name to that biography and gives him 36 votes, which is the by-election run (ninth of ten). No one else in the release has the name. The 1999 Toronto Centre—Rosedale run and the 2026 University—Rosedale by-election run are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file gives Charles C. Van Tuinen, the Reform candidate in Eglinton—Lawrence (second of seven, 4,347 votes), as a millwright, and its 1997 file gives Charles Van Tuinen, the Reform candidate in Eglinton—Lawrence (fourth of five, 3,547 votes), as a millwright. The runs are also for the same office and party, in the riding and its successor of the same name, in consecutive general elections, under a name that no one else in the release has. The 1993 and 1997 Eglinton—Lawrence runs are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file gives Danny Red Goldstick, who ran without a party in York South—Weston (eleventh of eleven, 62 votes), as a university lecturer, and its 2000 file gives Danny Goldstick, the Communist candidate in Toronto Centre—Rosedale (eighth of nine, 121 votes), as a university teacher. The occupation is the same in both years, and Goldstick is a rare surname. The 1993 York South—Weston run and the 2000 Toronto Centre—Rosedale run are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's list of Ontario NDP candidates in the 1995 provincial election gives David Jacobs, a lawyer, as the candidate in St. Andrew—St. Patrick with 9,231 votes in third place, which is the 1995 run, and notes that he was the NDP candidate for St. Paul's in the 1993 federal election. Wikipedia's list of NDP candidates in the 1993 federal election says Jacobs received 2,641 votes, finishing fourth against the Liberal Barry Campbell, which is the 1993 St. Paul's run (fourth of twelve), and Elections Canada gives that candidate as a lawyer. The 1993 St. Paul's run and the 1995 St. Andrew—St. Patrick run are joined as one Person.

No source describes the provincial runs, so the join rests on the release's structural rules. Donalda Fredeen ran for the Natural Law Party in Beaches—Woodbine federally in October 1993 and provincially in June 1995, and in Beaches—East York provincially in June 1999 and federally in November 2000; each of these pairs is in a riding of the same name at both levels, no more than two years apart, for the federal and Ontario parties of one name. Her 1995 and 1999 provincial runs are also for the same office and party in consecutive elections, in Beaches-Woodbine and its successor Beaches—East York. Elections Canada gives the federal candidate as a homemaker in 1993 and a mother at home in 1997 and 2000. The name is uncommon and no other Person in the release has it. The 1995 Beaches-Woodbine and 1999 Beaches—East York provincial runs are joined to the Person that holds the 1993, 1997 and 2000 federal runs.

Wikipedia's list of Marxist-Leninist candidates in the 2006 federal election gives France Tremblay's electoral record, which includes 38 votes in Scarborough Centre in 1993 (ninth of ten), 113 in Scarborough East in 2000 (sixth of six), 112 in Etobicoke Centre in 2004 (fifth of five) and 117 in Etobicoke Centre in 2006 (sixth of six). Each total and placing matches the release. The 2004 and 2006 Etobicoke Centre runs are joined to the Person that holds the 1993 Scarborough Centre and 2000 Scarborough East runs.

Elections Canada's 1997 candidate file gives John N. McKay as the Liberal elected in Scarborough East (23,065 votes) and as a lawyer. Its 2000 file gives John McKay as the Liberal elected in Scarborough East (24,019 votes) and marks him as the incumbent, so he was the sitting member for the seat the 1997 run won, and its 2004 table again gives him as a lawyer. The 1997 Scarborough East run is joined to the Person that holds the 2000 Scarborough East run and the Scarborough—Guildwood runs from 2004 to 2021.

Wikipedia's list of NDP candidates in the 2000 federal election gives Jordan Berger, a manager and the husband of Marit Stiles, as the Davenport candidate with 3,457 votes in second place, which is the 2000 Davenport run. Wikipedia's list of Ontario NDP candidates in the 2003 provincial election gives Jordan Berger, a manager and the husband of Marit Stiles, as the Davenport candidate with 7,243 votes in second place, which is the 2003 run, and Stiles's biography says her husband ran for the NDP in Davenport in 2003 and lost to Tony Ruprecht. The 2000 federal and 2003 provincial Davenport runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's page on the 2014 Toronto election gives Mary Hynes 3,953 votes in Ward 34 (Don Valley East), the 2014 run, and describes her as a former provincial and federal NDP candidate and a retired schoolteacher. A 2014 blog profile of the Ward 34 candidate says she had run at the provincial and federal levels and in a 2012 school board by-election, the TDSB Ward 17 run already in her Person, and that she taught elementary school in Scarborough for 25 years. The only provincial and federal runs by a Mary Hynes in the release are Mary Trapani Hynes's NDP runs in Don Valley East, and the Toronto Star's 2007 profile describes that candidate as a retired teacher. The 2012 TDSB Ward 17 and 2014 Ward 34 runs are joined to the Person that holds the 2007 provincial and the 2008 and 2011 federal Don Valley East runs.

Elections Ontario gives Nancy Kaur Ghuman as the Green Party of Ontario candidate in Etobicoke North in the 2018 provincial election, and Elections Canada gives Nancy Ghuman, an energy analyst, as the Green Party of Canada candidate in Etobicoke North in the 2019 federal election. The link rests on the release's rule for runs at both levels in one riding: the runs are no more than two years apart, the candidate ran for the federal and Ontario parties of one name, the name is uncommon, and no other Person in the release has it. The 2018 provincial and 2019 federal Etobicoke North runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's page on the 2003 Toronto election says the mayoral candidate Paul Lewin is a criminal lawyer who had campaigned for the Marijuana Party of Canada in the 2000 federal election, and gives him 271 votes, which is the 2003 mayoral run. Elections Canada's 2000 candidate file gives Paul Lewin, a lawyer, as the Marijuana Party candidate in Trinity—Spadina (fifth of nine, 673 votes), and he is the only candidate of that name in the file. The 2000 Trinity—Spadina run and the 2003 mayoral run are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's profile of the Don Mills candidates of 2 June 1995 describes the Liberal Richard Gosling, 47, as the head of North York's race relations committee and the owner of a landscaping business, which is the 1995 Don Mills run (second of seven, 7,607 votes). The Star of 3 September 1992 names Richard Gosling as one of the founders of the breakfast club and director of the city's race relations committee. The Star's editorial of 6 October 2010 says the Ward 12 York South-Weston candidate Rick Gosling founded the Toronto Children's Breakfast Club in 1984, which is the 2010 Ward 12 run (fifth of seven, 1,073 votes). The 1992 article ties the 1995 candidate's committee post to the founder of the breakfast club named in 2010. The 1995 Don Mills run and the 2010 Ward 12 run are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada's 1997 candidate file gives Shodja Ziaian, the NDP candidate in Don Valley East (fourth of seven, 2,981 votes), as a professor, and its 2019 candidate table gives Shodja Ziaian, an independent in Willowdale (seventh of seven, 71 votes), as a semi-retired university professor. The occupation is the same in both runs, and no one else in the release has this rare name. The 1997 Don Valley East run and the 2019 Willowdale run are joined as one Person.

Vaughan Byrnes ran for the Freedom Party of Ontario in Willowdale in the 1999 and 2003 provincial elections, on the same boundaries and with no general election between, and no source describes either candidate. The runs are for the same office, riding and party under an uncommon name that no one else in the release has, so same-office continuity applies. The 1999 and 2003 Willowdale runs are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's report of 25 June 2004 on the Scarborough—Agincourt race, read in ProQuest, covers the Conservative candidate Andrew Faust and says he finished a distant second behind Jim Karygiannis in the 2000 election as the candidate of the former Canadian Alliance. The official results give Andrew Faust as the Canadian Alliance candidate in Scarborough—Agincourt in 2000, second of six behind Karygiannis with 5,100 votes, and as the Conservative candidate there in 2004, second of five with 8,649 votes. No other candidate of that name appears in the release or in Elections Canada's 2000 candidate list. The 2000 and 2004 Scarborough—Agincourt runs are joined.

Robert Fulford's National Post column of 22 May 2004 names Barry Cline as the Conservative candidate for Parliament in St. Paul's, which is the 2004 run, second of four with 11,226 votes. It says Cline first ran when St. Paul's had no Tory candidate after the 2000 election was called, and that Carolyn Bennett beat him by 15,000 votes; the official 2000 results give Bennett 25,358 votes and the Progressive Conservative Barry Cline 10,099, second of nine. The column calls him an architect, and Elections Canada lists him as an architect in both 2000 and 2004. The 2000 and 2004 St. Paul's runs are joined.

Elections Ontario gives Birinder S Ahluwalia as an independent candidate in Willowdale in the 2018 provincial election, sixth of six with 233 votes, and Elections Canada gives Birinder Singh Ahluwalia as an independent in Willowdale in the 2015 and 2019 federal elections. The 2018 provincial and 2019 federal runs are 16 months apart in ridings of the same name, both without a party, under an uncommon name that no other Person in the release has, which meets the rule for runs at both levels in one riding. Elections Ontario also gives Birinder Singh Ahluwalia as an independent in Willowdale in 2022. That run follows the 2018 run in the same office and riding at the next general election, under the same uncommon name, with no other candidate of that name, which meets same-office continuity. No source describes him beyond the result listings. The 2018 and 2022 Willowdale provincial runs are joined to the Person holding the 2015 and 2019 Willowdale federal runs.

Wikipedia's article on Chris Lea, leader of the Green Party of Canada from 1990 to 1996, says he received 613 votes and finished sixth in Trinity—Spadina in the 1993 federal election and received 241 votes as the Green Party of Ontario candidate in St. George—St. David in the 1995 provincial election, matching both records. It describes him as a former professional architect, and Elections Canada lists the 1993 Green candidate as an architect. The 1993 Trinity—Spadina and 1995 St. George—St. David runs are joined.

Elections Ontario gives Constantine Kritsonis as the Green Party of Ontario candidate in York Centre in the 2003 provincial election, fourth of four with 1,496 votes. Elections Canada gives him as the Green Party of Canada candidate in York Centre in the 2004 federal election, a run on the Person that holds his other federal York Centre runs, his 1995 Oakwood run and his 1997 trustee run. The 2003 and 2004 runs are under nine months apart in ridings of the same name, for the Ontario and federal Green parties, under a rare name that no other Person in the release has, which meets the rule for runs at both levels in one riding. The Danforth Greens profile of Kritsonis lists his 1995 Oakwood campaign and his federal York Centre campaigns but does not mention the 2003 provincial run. The 2003 York Centre provincial run is joined to the Person holding his York Centre federal runs.

Wikipedia's article on David Berlin, read in its Wikiwand copy, says he was the New Democratic Party's candidate in Toronto Centre in the 2000 federal election and that in 2015 he founded and led the Bridge Party of Canada and ran as its candidate in University—Rosedale. The riding was named Toronto Centre—Rosedale in 2000, when the NDP's David Berlin placed third of nine, and the Bridge Party's David Berlin placed eighth of nine in University—Rosedale in 2015. The article describes him as editor and owner of the Literary Review of Canada from 1998 to 2001, and Elections Canada gives the 2000 candidate's occupation as editor of the Literary Review of Canada. The 2000 Toronto Centre—Rosedale and 2015 University—Rosedale runs are joined.

NOW Magazine's article of 6 January 2014 profiles Diana-De Maxted as a candidate for mayor and says this would be her third run, after bids in 2000 with 2,128 votes and 2006 with 1,311 votes, the totals of the 2000 and 2006 mayoral records. Wikipedia's page on the 2014 Toronto mayoral election lists Diana-De Maxted among the registered candidates, says she ran for mayor in 2000 and 2006 and for Toronto's 31st council ward in a 2001 by-election, and gives Diana Maxted 117 votes in its results, which is the 2014 record. The Globe and Mail's 2014 article on fringe candidates also says 2014 was her third run for mayor, after 2000 and 2006. The 2014 mayoral run and the December 2001 Ward 31 by-election run are joined to the Person holding her 2000 and 2006 mayoral runs.

The Toronto Star's profiles of the Scarborough West candidates in June 1995, read in ProQuest, describe the independent candidate Frank Meyers as a 48-year-old security administrator who lost his bid for office in the last federal election. That is the 1995 record, where Frank Meyers ran without a party and placed fifth of seven. Elections Canada's 1993 results list one Frank Meyers in the country, the Reform Party candidate in Broadview—Greenwood, third of nine with 4,356 votes, and give his occupation as security administrator. The 1995 Scarborough West provincial run is joined to the 1993 Broadview—Greenwood federal run.

Wikipedia's list of New Democratic Party candidates in the 2004 federal election gives Greg Gogan in Scarborough Centre with 6,156 votes, 16.82 per cent and third place, matching the 2004 record. Its notes say he led Option Canada from 1991 to 1993 and was the National Party candidate for Scarborough West in the 1993 federal election, which is the 1993 record, fifth of eight with 578 votes. Elections Canada gives the 1993 candidate's occupation as political organizer. The 1993 Scarborough West and 2004 Scarborough Centre runs are joined.

blogTO's preview of the Parkdale—High Park race, posted on 8 October 2008, names Jilian Saweczko as the Conservative candidate, which is the 2008 record, and says she had run and lost in the riding before. The only earlier run under that name in Parkdale—High Park, at any level in the release, is the 1997 Progressive Conservative run, third of eight with 5,926 votes. Elections Canada gives her occupation as independent businesswoman in 1997 and as entrepreneur in 2008 and 2011. The 1997 Parkdale—High Park run is joined to the Person holding the 2008 Parkdale—High Park and 2011 York South—Weston runs.

The City of Toronto's results give Julien Baeta as a candidate for Conseil scolaire Viamonde trustee in Ward 2 in 2010, third of three, in Ward 2 in 2014, when he was elected, and again in 2018. The city wards that made up Ward 2 in 2010 all fall within Ward 2 as drawn for 2014, so the 2010 ward lies wholly inside the 2014 one. The 2010 and 2014 runs are for the same office at consecutive elections, under an uncommon name that no one else in the release has, with no competing candidate of that name, which meets same-office continuity. The 2010 Ward 2 run is joined to the Person holding the 2014 and 2018 Ward 2 runs.

Wikipedia's list of independent candidates in the 1995 Ontario election has a section on Linda Dale Gibbons, the St. George—St. David candidate. Its electoral record gives her 1993 federal run in Rosedale for Ken Campbell's Christian Freedom Party, with 214 votes and eighth of ten, and her 1995 independent run in St. George—St. David, with 326 votes and fourth of seven, matching both records. It says she was running in the 2014 Trinity—Spadina federal by-election under her legal name, Linda Groce, and lists that run for the Christian Heritage Party; the record gives the Christian Heritage candidate as Linda Groce-Gibbons. The section says she worked at an anti-abortion pregnancy centre in the early 1990s, and Elections Canada gives the 1993 candidate's occupation as crisis pregnancy counsellor. The 1993 Rosedale, 1995 St. George—St. David and 2014 Trinity—Spadina runs are joined.

The Toronto Star's candidate profiles of 5 June 1995, read in ProQuest, describe Marilyn Pepper, 44, the Natural Law Party candidate, as in business and running on much the same platform she used in the 1993 federal election. That is the 1995 York East record, sixth of six with 243 votes. Elections Canada's 1993 results list one Marilyn Pepper in the country, the Natural Law Party candidate in Etobicoke North, and give her occupation as businessperson. The 1995 York East provincial run is joined to the Person holding the 1993 and 1997 Etobicoke North federal runs.

Elections Ontario gives Neil Spiegel as the Green Party of Ontario candidate in Parkdale—High Park in the 2003 provincial election, fourth of eight with 2,758 votes. Elections Canada gives him as the Green Party of Canada candidate in Parkdale—High Park in 2000 and in 2004, and the 2004 run, under nine months after the provincial one, belongs to the Person holding the 2000 run. The 2003 and 2004 runs are in ridings of the same name, for the Ontario and federal Green parties, under an uncommon name that no other Person in the release has, which meets the rule for runs at both levels in one riding. No other source describes him. The 2003 Parkdale—High Park provincial run is joined to the Person holding the 2000 and 2004 Parkdale—High Park federal runs.

Wikipedia's biography of Patrick Boyer says he was elected for Etobicoke—Lakeshore as a Progressive Conservative in 1984 and was not re-elected in the 1993 general election, and that he was nominated again as the Conservative candidate for Etobicoke—Lakeshore and lost the 2008 election to Michael Ignatieff. Its results tables give Boyer 14,306 votes in Etobicoke—Lakeshore in 1993 and 17,793 in 2008, the totals of the two records. It gives his profession as lawyer and writer, and Elections Canada lists the 1993 candidate as an author and lawyer. The 1993 and 2008 Etobicoke—Lakeshore runs are joined.

The Freedom Party of Ontario's biography of its leader says Paul McKeever first ran for the party in Ontario's 1999 election, and the party's release of 19 August 2009 names him as its candidate in the 17 September 2009 St. Paul's by-election. An archived copy of Wikipedia's biography of Paul McKeever gives his 1999 run in Toronto Centre—Rosedale with 344 votes and his 2009 St. Paul's by-election run with 61 votes, the totals of the two records. The 1999 Toronto Centre—Rosedale and 2009 St. Paul's runs are joined.

The Toronto Star's report of 28 November 2000 on the Etobicoke Centre result describes Ross Vaughan as a 50-year-old realtor running for the Tories, which is the 2000 Progressive Conservative run, third of five; Elections Canada gives his occupation as real estate sales person. The Star's council candidate profiles of 9 November 2006, under Ward 3 Etobicoke Centre, describe Ross Vaughan as a realtor who would extend the subway to the Mississauga border, which is the 2006 Ward 3 run. Ward 3 lies within the Etobicoke Centre federal riding. The 2000 Etobicoke Centre federal run is joined to the Person holding the 2003, 2006 and 2010 Ward 3 council runs.

The House of Commons page on Sarmite Bulte lists her general election candidacies in Parkdale—High Park: elected on 2 June 1997, re-elected on 27 November 2000 and 28 June 2004, and defeated on 23 January 2006. Those are the four records, which give her as the Liberal candidate each time. Wikipedia's biography says she was defeated by the New Democrat Peggy Nash in January 2006 and gives her 20,676 votes in 2000, the record's total. The 1997, 2000, 2004 and 2006 Parkdale—High Park runs are joined.

Elections Ontario gives Silvio Ursomarzo as the Freedom Party of Ontario candidate in Trinity—Spadina in the 1999 provincial election, seventh of eight with 182 votes, and Sylvio Ursomarzo as the party's candidate in Trinity—Spadina in 2007, eighth of eight with 147 votes. The 2007 run belongs to the Person that also holds his 2003, 2006 and 2011 Freedom Party runs. The two Trinity—Spadina runs are for the same office and party in a riding of the same name, with one general election between them, under a rare name that no one else in the release has and with no competing candidate of that name, which meets same-office continuity. The 1999 Trinity—Spadina run is joined to the Person holding the 2003 to 2011 runs.

The Toronto Star's profiles of the Willowdale candidates of 22 October 1993, read in ProQuest, describe the Green candidate Tom Salsberg as a former elementary teacher now studying psychotherapy, which is the 1993 federal record, sixth of nine. Its story on the Wilson Heights riding of 2 June 1995 describes the Green Party candidate Tom Salsberg as a 37-year-old psychotherapist and former NDP member, which is the 1995 provincial record, fifth of seven. Both profiles place him in psychotherapy, as a student in 1993 and as a practitioner in 1995. The 1993 Willowdale federal run and the 1995 Wilson Heights provincial run are joined.

The City of Toronto's results give Walied Khogali Ali as a candidate for council in Ward 13 (Toronto Centre) in 2018, fifth of 19, and in 2026, fourth of 11. The runs are for the same office in the same ward, with one general election between them, under a full name that no one else in the release has and with no competing candidate of that name, which meets same-office continuity. The Toronto Star's profile of 1 May 2026 describes the 2026 candidate as an organizer and social advocate who sits on council's confronting anti-Black racism advisory committee, but it does not mention 2018. The 2018 and 2026 Ward 13 runs are joined.

The Local's 2026 guide to Ward 24 (Scarborough-Guildwood), in its school trustee section added on 14 October 2026, lists Darren Frake among the nine TDSB candidates in this contest. It describes him as a principal at Canada International College who joined the school as a teacher in 2010, and says he ran for trustee in Ward 20 in the 2022 municipal election, placing second of four candidates. The City's 2022 results give Darren Frake second of four in TDSB Ward 20 with 1,561 votes, the run held by the target. The 2026 TDSB Ward 12 run joins the Person holding the 2022 Ward 20 run.

The Local's 2026 guide to Ward 5 (York South-Weston), in its school trustee section added on 14 October 2026, lists Sal Piccininni among the five TCDSB candidates in this contest. It describes him as a TTC operator who was previously a TCDSB trustee until 2018 and served as the board's vice-chair for two terms. The City's results give Sal Piccininni as the elected TCDSB trustee for Ward 3 in 1997, 2003, 2006, 2010 and 2014 and as runner-up there in 2018, the runs held by the target, and no other Piccininni has held a TCDSB seat. The guide calls his former ward Ward 10, the current number for York South-Weston, part of which lay in his Ward 3, and dates his service from 2000, where the record has a first election in 1997 and a council run in 2000. The 2026 TCDSB Ward 10 run joins the Person holding the 1997 to 2018 trustee runs.

The Local's 2026 guide to Ward 21 (Scarborough Centre), in its school trustee section added on 14 October 2026, lists Celine DiNova among the three TCDSB candidates in this contest. It says she is a retired secondary school teacher and that she ran for TCDSB trustee in Ward 11 in 2022, placing second of four candidates. The City's 2022 results give Celine Dinova second of four in TCDSB Ward 11 with 2,447 votes, the run held by the target. The 2026 TCDSB Ward 7 run joins the Person holding the 2022 Ward 11 run.

The Local's 2026 guide to Ward 14 (Toronto-Danforth), in its school trustee section added on 14 October 2026, lists Gus Stefanis among the nine TDSB candidates in this contest. It describes him as the former leader of the Canadian Nationalist Party and says that the year before he ran for trustee in Ward 11, Don Valley West, losing to Stacey Cline. The City's results for the TDSB Ward 11 by-election of 3 March 2025 give Stacey Cline as the winner and Gus Stefanis eighth of ten, the target's run, and the target's 2019 and 2021 Scarborough—Guildwood runs were for the Nationalist party. The 2026 TDSB Ward 5 run joins the Person holding the 2019, 2021 and 2025 runs.

The Toronto Star's Scarborough Centre candidate profiles of 22 October 1993 describe the Libertarian candidate George Dance as an office and sales manager who has been active in his party since 1974, most recently as national party leader, which is the 1993 Scarborough Centre run (eighth of ten, 153 votes); Elections Canada gives that candidate as an office manager. The Star's Scarborough West profiles of 2 June 1995 describe the Libertarian candidate George Dance as 'the former leader of its federal party' and a 41-year-old computer products office manager who has run at both levels without success, which is the 1995 Scarborough West run (sixth of seven, 214 votes). A biography of George J. Dance gives his birth in October 1953, office manager among his occupations and his leadership of the Libertarian Party of Canada from 1991 to May 1993. The 1993 Scarborough Centre run is joined to the Person that holds the 1995 Scarborough West run and the 1996 York South by-election run.

The Toronto Star's candidate profiles of 5 June 1995 describe the High Park-Swansea Green candidate David G. Burman, 50, as a dentist and university professor, which is the 1995 High Park-Swansea run (fourth of five, 368 votes). Elections Canada's 1997 candidate list gives the Green candidate David Burman in Etobicoke—Lakeshore as a dentist, which is the 1997 run (sixth of eight, 315 votes). Both sources give the same occupation, and the two ridings are neighbours in the west end of the city. The 1995 High Park-Swansea run is joined to the Person that holds the 1997 Etobicoke—Lakeshore run.

The Toronto Star's candidate profiles of 5 June 1995 describe the Fort York Libertarian candidate Paul N.G. Barker, 35, as a printer making his third run for a provincial seat, which is the 1995 Fort York run (fifth of eight, 266 votes). Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file gives the Libertarian candidate Paul Barker in Trinity—Spadina as a printer, which is the 1993 run (eighth of ten, 290 votes). Both sources give the same trade for runs 19 months apart in nearby downtown ridings, and no other Paul Barker is in the release. The 1993 Trinity—Spadina run is joined to the Person that holds the 1995 Fort York run.

The Toronto Star's council candidate profiles of 9 November 2006 describe the Ward 7 York West candidate Sandra Anthony as a former employee of the World Health Organization, now a nutritionist and community activist, which is the 2006 Ward 7 run (second of four, 2,753 votes). Elections Canada gives the New Democratic candidate Sandra Romano Anthony in York West as a nutritionist in 2004 and 2006, which are the 2004 run (second of five, 4,228 votes) and the 2006 run (third of five, 4,724 votes). Ward 7 is one of the two council wards formed from the York West riding, and the council run came ten months after the second federal run. The 2006 Ward 7 run is joined to the Person that holds the 2004 and 2006 York West federal runs.

The Toronto Star's Scarborough school board candidate profiles of 10 November 1994 describe the Ward 11 candidate Laura-Maria Nikolareizi as a former constituency worker for a local MP, which is the 1994 Scarborough Board of Education Ward 11 run (fourth of seven, 327 votes); the Star's results of 16 November 1994 print the same name for that run, which the City's archive prints as Laura-Marie. The Star's report of 7 November 2003 says Nikolareizi, 33, has worked as an assistant to Mayor Mel Lastman and Scarborough MP Jim Karygiannis, which is the 2003 Ward 37 Scarborough Centre run (third of seven, 1,156 votes), and The Local's 2022 Ward 10 guide calls her a former aide to Karygiannis, the MP for Scarborough-Agincourt, who ran in Scarborough Centre in 2003. Both Star articles describe work on the staff of a Scarborough MP, and no one else in the release has the surname. The 1994 Scarborough Board of Education Ward 11 run is joined to the Person that holds the 2003 Ward 37 and 2022 Ward 10 council runs.

Elections Canada's 1993 candidate file gives the Marxist-Leninist candidate Julie Northrup in Etobicoke—Lakeshore as a sales representative, which is the 1993 run (eighth of nine, 78 votes); the Toronto Star's Etobicoke Lakeshore profiles of 22 October 1993 describe the same candidate as a printing company executive. The Star's candidate profiles of 5 June 1995 describe the independent candidate Julie Northrup, 40, as a sales rep, which is the 1995 Etobicoke-Lakeshore provincial run (sixth of six, 186 votes). Elections Canada's 1993 record and the Star's 1995 profile give the same occupation for runs 19 months apart in the riding of the same name, and no one else in the release has the name. The 1993 Etobicoke—Lakeshore federal run is joined to the Person that holds the 1995 Etobicoke-Lakeshore provincial run.

The Toronto Star's Wilson Heights candidate profiles of 2 June 1995 describe the Natural Law candidate Mike Dubinsky as a 39-year-old accounting and software consultant, which is the 1995 Wilson Heights run (fourth of seven, 438 votes); the profile also calls him new to politics. Elections Canada gives the Natural Law candidate Mike Dubinsky in York Centre in 1997 as a computer consultant, and the Star's 1997 York Centre profile says he works in automated finance administration, which is the 1997 run (sixth of eight, 242 votes). Elections Canada and the Star's 1993 profile give the 1993 Willowdale Natural Law candidate as a finance administrator. The 1995 occupation matches the computing and finance work given for the 1997 run and fits the 1993 finance work, so the profile's statement that he was new to politics, which conflicts with the 1993 run, is treated as an error. The 1995 Wilson Heights run is joined to the Person that holds the 1993 Willowdale and 1997 York Centre runs.

Wikipedia's list of Marxist-Leninist candidates in the 2006 federal election gives Rutchinski's electoral record with the 1993 Rosedale (61 votes), 1997 Toronto Centre—Rosedale (166), 1999 Beaches—East York provincial (164) and 2000 Beaches—East York (53) runs, which match the release, and his 2004 and 2006 runs in Nickel Belt, and says that, formerly a steelworker, shipping supervisor and truck driver, he works at the University of Toronto as of 2005. Elections Canada gives the 2006 Nickel Belt candidate Steve Rutchinski as university administrative staff and the 2008 and 2011 Nickel Belt candidate as a university administrator. It gives the 2015 University—Rosedale candidate as a university administrator, in the same French wording as in 2006, the 2019 University—Rosedale candidate as a university administrator in graduate studies and the 2025 Beaches—East York candidate as a post-secondary education administrator. Elections Canada's earlier entries, shipping supervisor in 1993, truck driver in 1997 and industrial worker in 2000, agree with the Wikipedia note, and no one else in the release has the surname. The Person that holds the 2015 and 2019 University—Rosedale and 2025 Beaches—East York runs is joined to the Person that holds the 1993, 1997 and 2000 federal runs and the 1999 provincial run.

The Legislative Assembly of Ontario's member page for Joseph Cordiano gives him as an Ontario Liberal member from 1985 until he resigned on September 22, 2006. It lists him as the member for Lawrence in the 36th Parliament, from June 8, 1995 to June 2, 1999, and for York South—Weston in the 37th Parliament, from June 3, 1999, and the 38th Parliament, from October 2, 2003. Those terms begin on the polling days of the 1995 Lawrence run, where the record has him elected for the Liberals with 11,784 votes, first of five, and of the 1999 and 2003 York South—Weston runs, where he was elected for the Ontario Liberal Party. His Wikipedia biography gives his constituency as Lawrence from 1987 to 1999 and says the 1995 election saw him win his riding by a comfortable margin. It says that in 1999 he sought the Liberal nomination in the redistributed riding of York South—Weston and won an easy victory in the election that followed, and that he won another easy victory there in 2003. Its electoral tables give him 18,205 votes in 1999 and 19,932 in 2003, which match the 1999 record, first of eight, and the 2003 record, first of five. Elections Ontario's 1999 results mark the York South—Weston candidate, printed as Joe Cordiano, as a member of the previous legislature, which agrees with the Lawrence seat the Legislative Assembly gives him in the 36th Parliament. The 1995 Lawrence run and the 1999 and 2003 York South—Weston runs are joined as one Person.
